description: A soak buys time for someone else to hit the bug first; its length is how long the ecosystem
needs to absorb a breaking release and the vendor needs to ship a regression patch. All
release-age policy lives here; this preset is extended LAST in renovate.json:
minimumReleaseAge is a plain scalar, so the last matching rule wins, and the two rules below
that remove a soak must beat every earlier setter (the shared preset's per-update-type ladder,
override-calver's flat 14 days). Keep this entry last in extends; add new release-age rules
here so nothing earlier silently outranks them.
A regressing Longhorn patch reaches every PersistentVolume's data and does not roll back like
it rolls forward; seven days, not the ladder's one, lets someone else flag it first. By
convention, not this rule, the maintainer adopts a release line only after its first patch.
Both spellings: the flux manager emits the chart name, the custom.regex annotations the
GitHub slug.
A Longhorn or KubeVirt minor is a breaking release (override-breaking-changes.json marks
both): thirty days gives dependents time to catch up and the vendor time to patch
regressions. Coder is soaked for a different reason: it ships stable and experimental
releases on one channel, and a release only counts as stable after roughly a month, so the
soak reconstructs that unpublished stable channel.
Images this repo builds itself (docker.io/ppatlabs/*) are adopted as soon as published:
the someone-else a soak waits for does not exist for a first-party build. Not a claim our
images are safer.
No matchUpdateTypes: an unlisted type would stay soaked by whatever set it last. null is
the unset spelling; read it as zero (Renovate has no literal zero).
Both spellings (registry-prefixed as the kubernetes manager emits, bare for annotations):
a matcher matching nothing raises no error -- the previous glob was inert for two years
(#3795); the idiom takes NO slash before the brace.
A digest refresh means the tag this repo runs was repointed at a rebuilt image (usually a
CVE rebuild, the last thing to sit on); the version decision was taken when the tag was
adopted. Soaking it is a trap, not a delay: Renovate ages the refresh against the tag's
last repoint, so an image rebuilt more often than the soak never clears it, and under
internalChecksFilter 'strict' the held branch is never created (no PR, no error); a tag
with no release timestamp is held forever.
Repo-wide because every docker dep is digest-pinned and an allowlist would not protect the
next mutable tag added; docker-only because the github-actions SHA-pin soaks guard against
tags moved to hostile code and must not be swept up.
Digest updates only; version soaks and first-time pinning untouched. Ordering is
load-bearing (file note above).
